title: The Twice-Written Card
request: Total the days lent to registered borrowers — one number. Mind the register: a clerk has been known to write the same card on two lines, and I will not be billed twice for one book.
objective: Avoid duplicate keys in the right table multiplying the rows a join returns.
hints: A card written on two register lines gives every one of its slips two partners.
The days live entirely in the slips; the register is only being asked whether a card is known.
Keep the slips whose card is contained in the register's card column and add up their days column, without ever building the joined table.
inputCode:
import random
from datascience import Table, make_array
names = ['Gideon Plume', 'Halla Brine', 'Isolde Marrow', 'Jarek Quill']
cards = [107, 108, 109, 110]
size = random.randint(2, 4)
chosen = sorted(random.sample(range(4), size))
register_cards = [cards[index] for index in chosen]
register_names = [names[index] for index in chosen]
repeats = random.randint(0, 2)
for _ in range(repeats):
    index = random.choice(chosen)
    register_cards.append(cards[index])
    register_names.append(names[index])
register = Table().with_columns('card', make_array(*register_cards), 'name', make_array(*register_names))
n = random.randint(3, 6)
slips = Table().with_columns('card', make_array(*[cards[random.choice(chosen)] for _ in range(n)]), 'days', make_array(*[random.randint(1, 25) for _ in range(n)]))
